Halfen has confirmed "the HTA 50/30 and the HZA 53/34 are equivalent in quality and material. The HZA 53/34 has additional load capacity so the performance would be higher in that sense." records.description: The civil curves need to be designed to accommodate a normally operating train (also called the Normal LRV Model) which assumes curve entry speed equals cab speed. This should allow for a 20mph code to be provided on a 20mph curve, however, when the train is in the curve the train could go into a braking profile and when that occurs we need to use the Safe Braking LRV Model which requires no more than 4.5” of unbalanced super (Eu). This requirement is in accordance with DCM5-14.4.6.D, see below for excerpt. D. Block layout in approach to curves shall slow normally operating trains to the design speed calculated in accordance with Chapter 4. Also, no train operating on Safe Braking Distance parameters shall exceed 4.5 inchesofunbalancedsuperelevation. The unbalance for each curve on R200 has been checked against an overspeed of 4 mph greater than the current design speed for each curve, and the resultant unbalance has been confirmed to be less than 4.5” except for curves EB 312B and WB 312. If we look at modifying the track geometry to mitigate the overspeed unbalance limits we also run up against the limits of the DCM. records.title: R200-REC-04853 RFI 00129 Discontinued Cobranet PA Microphone.pdf
records.description: As previously discussed with Sound Transit the BiAmp Audia PA equipment series has gone End-of-Life. SWK placed an order for all equipment prior to this happening, however the NPS-1 microphone went End of Life prior to all other products and this order is unable to be filled. SWK also attempted to buy this product on the secondary market and it was unavailable. BiAmp does not make another compatible Cobranet Micorphone in the Audia Series. SWK EOR and team have identified two options available to remedy this situation: 1. SWK can proceed with the BiAmp Vocia microphone that uses a Cobranet media converter to be comparable with the existing AudiaFlex system. The functionality of the system will be the same but an additional piece of rack mounted equipment is required for each microphone. 2. SWK can modify the design to use an analog paging station rather than a CobraNet digital product. This will involve some modification to the architecture of the PA system around the connection of the microphones and the DSP. Currently the microphones connect through a PA switch and then to the DSP, this would need to be changed so the microphones connect directly to the DSP through additional analog expansion module inputs. An analog paging station has a different form factor that neworked paging mics, see attached Astatic cutsheet. There is additional cost associated with the additional equipment and design work for both options. An approximate ROM cost for either option is around $15,000. Risks associated with option 1 include the Vocia being a new product to Sound Transit. Risks associated with option 2 include schedule risk due to design rework and mitigation of cross talk issues with an analog microphone. Please advise which option Sound Transit would like to proceed with.

records.title: R200-REC-05333 RFI 00135 Specification Compliant BDA Product.pdf
records.description: The Radio design has been under evaluation regarding the supply voltage to the Radio BBUs and BDAs. History: At the beginning of this design build contract, the understood to be preferred BDA vendor, Cobham was an active supplier of the BDA equipment this project required. In December 2020, Cobham went into "Administration". This was brought to the attention of the project team and discussions with SWK and the DBPM resulted in the designs (and subsequently the shop drawings) that implemented Axell Wireless (formerly Cobham) products. Since these discussions, the former Cobham products has undergone multiple manufacturers names and is currently being provided by the supplier PBE Axell. During the progression of the design and shop level drawings it has been made clear that Sound Transit will not accept the use of DC powered BDAs. After eveuilation of the Sound Transit comments, Day Wireless Systems (DWS), Modern Communications Systems (MCS) subcontractor worked with the PBE Axell to provide a compliant BDA. DWS received confirmation on 12/22/21 (Attachment A) that PBE Axell would produce a custom 800MHz Class A BDA to meet the following requirements: frequency band, input voltage type and connector type. On 04/14/22 PBE Axell notified DWS that they will no longer be able to uphold the commitment to meet the input voltage or connector type (Attachment B). Request: As a design build team, the following three options are being proposed for Sound Transit to provide direction: 1. Move forward with PBE Axell (to date, the known preferred vendor) and allow the use of DC service voltage Class A 800MHz BDAs. 1.a. Only the BDA input voltage with DC; devices on the line side of the BDA are assumed to be fed with AC (TPSS locations excluded). 1.b. Spec deviations are outlined in Attachment C. These will also need to be considered acceptable if staying with PBE Axell *Preferred Solution* 2. Provide direction to deviate from the preferred vendor and go with a new one. 2.a. MCS and DWS recommend Fiplex with the below listed understandings. 2.a.1. If chosen to go with Fiplex, a single, dual band, AC feed BDA will replace the current design that utilizes two (2) BDAs (one for 700MHz band and one for 800MHz band) which is permitted by 27 60 02 2.09 D. 1. 2.a.2. Spec deviations are outlined in Attachment C. These will also need to be considered acceptable if going with Fiplex. 3. Sound Transit to identify a different preferred vendor along with the Sound Transit permissible spec deviations.

records.title: R200-REC-11939 RFI 00282 SIT 301 OCS Live Wire Test - Performing Testing with Siemens LRV.pdf
records.description: Change Order 115 included direction to perform (and, implicitly, obtain passing results for) SIT 301/302 OCS Live Wire testing utilizing both the Kinkisharyo and Siemens vehicles. During the same efforts on the Lynnwood Link Extension project, it was observed that there were no substantial operational differences between the two vehicle types that impacted their performance in relation to the OCS interface. As a result, the project team made the decision to consolidate the Kinkisharyo and Siemens Live Wire test results into a single passing result. This consolidated result was subsequently approved by Sound Transit, paving the way for the recommendation to transition into Pre-Revenue operations. The successful completion of these tests and the subsequent acceptance by Sound Transit were critical milestones in the project's development and demonstrated the readiness of the OCS for revenue operation. MEC recommends that it not be required to obtain separate passing test results with both Kinkisharyo and Siemens vehicles when interfacing with the Overhead Contact System (OCS). This recommendation stems from extensive evaluations demonstrating no significant performance discrepancies between the two vehicle types during OCS interactions. MEC's thorough testing procedures have revealed that both Kinkisharyo and Siemens vehicles exhibit consistent and satisfactory performance with the OCS. The absence of notable differences in their behavior supports the conclusion that testing of both types can be combined without compromising safety or operational efficiency.

records.title: R200-REC-12240 RFI 00296 EP29 ERCES TDI Mitigation.pdf
records.description: As part of the initial energizing of the active ERCES equipment within EP29, Day Wireless conducted an organic Public Safety coverage evaluation of the over the air PSERN signals being received within the EP29 ERCES coverage footprint, including the E30 Comms House, and E30 TPSS. Appendix A (see attached) shows details from the organic signal testing at the EP29 DRLE garage complex. Every grid tested passed with 5 exceptions: 1. The TPSS had a signal of -115, unable to get a admit tone on the radio.. DAQ of less than 2. (See red boxes, Appendix A1) 2. First Floor room in grid 17 had a signal of -102 and a DAQ of 2.5. (See red boxes, Appendix A2) 3. First floor Fire Pump & Riser Room EP29P07 had a signal of -114 but access to the PSERN system was achieved and a DAQ of 3.4 was attained. (See red boxes, Appendix A2) 4. Comms House had a signal of -104 but access to the PSERN system was achieved and a DAQ of 3.4 was attained. (See Appendix A3) 5. Level 2 Comm Closet EP29L202 (headend room) had a signal of -100, but access to the PSERN system was achieved and a DAQ of 3.4 was attained. (See Appendix A4) The rest of the rooms tested with DAQ of 3.4 or better. (See Appendix 5-8) As you look at the grids please note that any grid that contained a room, the room was tested with the door closed and the results were what was recorded on the form. Signal level testing was done with an Anritsu S412E using a PSERN provided antenna and 10 sample averaging on the PSERN North simulcast control channel. DAQ testing was between a radio in either the center of the grid, or the center of any room that was in the grid. DAQ testing was performed with APX 6000 radios supplied by PSERN with one user on-site in each grid, and one user at the DWS shop in SeaTac, WA. Appendix B indicates steps required to mitigate the TDI issue. DWS contends that left unmitigated, the EP29 ERCES introduces significant dominance over macro TDI issues within the coverage footprint of the SERG as well as a significant TDI envelope external to the SERG that will create significant communications issues for the AHJ when responding to the area immediately surrounding the SERG. Appendix C shows sketches of the proposed TDI Mitigation efforts as described in Appendix B, superimposed on images of the System Riser Diagram and First Floor design. DWS proposes the TDI mitigation efforts as summarized in Appendix B. Complete cost and schedule impacts cannot be fully assessed at this time. Once there is concurrence on the proposed approach outlined in appendix B, cost and schedule impacts will be finalized and communicated to SWK.

records.title: R200-REC-12312A RFI 00299 E27 Pedestrian Crossing Operation II.pdf
records.description: The contractor has received the response provided in R200-REC-12089. The contractor is proposing to take the following actions to modify the E27 crossing design and associated documentation, at the request of Sound Transit. 1) Modify RTS-E ped crossing design with configurable "turn back operation mode" at Redmond Technology Station (RTS) pedestrian crossings. -turn back mode is enabled by a physical jumper adding voltage to a vital input on the SVP. If no voltage is detected at the designated input, turn back mode is disabled. -While in turn back mode, the eastbound cab speed code for EB7789T will be disabled 15 seconds after the train is fully berthed at the station (EB7723T vacant and EB7789T occupied). Once the eastbound cab speed code on EB7789T has been disabled, RTS-E ped crossing will recover. The crossing will reactivate if the island track circuit (EB7838RPT) is occupied. -While turn back mode is disabled, RTS-E crossing will have a standard operation and will remain active as long as the approach is occupied. -This change will require modification to the E27 signal house circuit plans, E27 application logic, signal system training material and development of crossing approach plans. 2) Development of crossing approach plans The contractor has informally received as-built crossing approach plans that encompass RTS-E and RTS-W ped crossings in PDF format, and has been requested to modify these plans in accordance with the R200 crossing design. The contractor requires the as-built CADD files to be provided by ST, or direction for the contractor to develop this document from scratch. The contractor has attached markups to the as-built drawings that indicate the changes proposed for the R200 design modifications. The contractor does not intend to include the Marymoor Village Station Ped Crossing (E30) in these approach plans unless directed by ST. The contractor requires concurrence from ST on all details outlined in this RFI to proceed with the actions proposed, and accurately assess cost and schedule impacts.

records.title: R200-REC-12820 RFI 00308 Garage - Elevators Sump Pump Power Source.pdf
records.description: Reference DCM 23.4.8.C.3, EP29-EPS954, INFORMATIONAL EP29-EPS955, HP-RFI-1552 Power routing for the elevator sump pumps is not able to be routed per current design due to the pumps being 20amp 1ph 120V and not 20amp 3ph 480V as indicated on EP29-PB4-01 as shown on EP29-EPS954. (This transformer is a 18-21 week lead time.) - This is a step-down transformer that would create a multiple circuit load center. - It could potentially be utilized if there are any additional circuits that need to be added before the end of the project. - Upsizing to a 55kVA transformer to feed panel EP29-PB2-01. (This transformer is a 18-21 week lead time.) - Would allow panel to be upsized to 150A. - Would also require upsizing the current 70A breaker in PB4-01 feeding T-01. - Potentially feeders to the transformer would need to be replaced as well. - Use EP29-PB2-02 by reducing the reserve spare conduits from 20% to 15% as shown on the INFORMATIONAL EP29-EPS955. Due to the long lead times of 18-21 weeks to procure additional transformers, we would like to reduce the reserve spare conduits from 20% to 15%.
